title: Duchy of Styria
capsule: The Duchy of Styria was elevated from a march to a duchy by Emperor Frederick Barbarossa in 1180, with Ottokar IV as its first duke; on Ottokar's death in 1192 it passed by the Georgenberg Pact to the Babenberg Dukes of Austria. Ottokar II of Bohemia seized it after the Battle of Kressenbrunn in 1260 but lost both Austria and Styria when Rudolf I of Habsburg defeated him at the Battle on the Marchfeld in 1278, beginning unbroken Habsburg rule. Styria thereafter formed a core component of the Inner Austrian lands, and Graz served as the capital of the Inner Austrian branch of the dynasty through the 16th and 17th centuries.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The duchy's core boundaries are well attested through Habsburg administrative records and cartography; the attestation window 1260–1502 covers the Přemyslid and early Habsburg periods, which are documented in both narrative and archival sources.
